title: Closing the global menu with the Esc key inappropriately triggers panel auto-hide when the cursor was still hovering over the panel
line: An auto-hide panel no longer hides when you close one of its menus (like the Global Menu) while the pointer is still on it.
explanation: When a menu opened from the panel grabs the pointer, Qt's Wayland plugin sends the panel a Leave event although the pointer is still on it, and when the menu closes it only sends the matching Enter back to xdg-shell windows, not to a layer-shell panel. PanelView then believed the pointer was gone and hid the panel as soon as the menu closed. The Global Menu also lost the panel as its transient parent: since its menu became a child of the application's hidden menu, QMenu replaces the transient parent with that hidden window when it is shown. The change makes PanelView ignore the one Leave sent while a popup whose transient parent is this panel is open, and keeps the panel as the Global Menu's transient parent (full and compact view) by no longer parenting the menu to the application's menu (it is still deleted with it).

commits.message:
shell/panelview: Ignore the Leave event sent when a panel menu opens

Qt sends a panel a Leave when its menu grabs the pointer, and no Enter
after it closes, so auto-hide hid the panel under the pointer. Ignore
that Leave, and keep the panel as the Global Menu's transient parent.

BUG: 473454

media.caption: Master, top auto-hide panel: File open from the Global Menu, then 0.6 s and 2 s after pressing Esc with the pointer still on File, then after moving off: the panel is gone right after Esc.
Patched: same steps, the panel stays under the pointer after Esc and hides once the pointer moves off it.
Master: closing the menu by clicking File again hides the panel under the pointer.
Patched: clicking File again closes the menu and the panel stays until the pointer leaves.
Master: clicking the clock while the menu is open closes the menu, and the panel hides under the pointer.
Patched: clicking the clock closes the menu and the panel stays under the pointer until it leaves.
